Event organizers expected 25,000 guests, but more than 45,000 showed up.

Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson hosted the free concert for military and Department of Defense I.D. cardholders.

Each member was allowed to sponsor up to 10 guests.

The all-star line up included celebrities like Nick Jonas, Kevin Hart, Jack Black and surfer Laird Hamilton.

Event organizers say it was on a first come first-served basis and weren't prepared to handle such a large crowd.

"I think in any situation when you have that many people its hard for 45,000 people to have the exact same experience," said Casey Patterson, executive producer of Rock the Troops. "What ended up happening is that the demand for the event was more than anyone anticipated."

Daily Devotional

October 24

10 For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.11 But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness. (1 Timothy 6:10-11 KJV)

Notice that it says “love of money” is the root of all evil, and it does not say that money is evil. The devil has led many to believe that money is evil, and that all rich people are therefore evil people, and that is not what the bible is saying. Many people have done evil things because of the desire for money, but money itself is not evil. Many people in the bible such as Abraham, David and Solomon were extremely rich, and were blessed by God in many ways, and were not basically evil people. Jesus taught that it was difficult for a rich man to enter heaven (Matthew 19:23-24). And although money is not evil, it can certainly become an idol and be worshiped as such, by those that have it, thereby making it hard for the rich to keep their focus upon Jesus, and not their riches.

This verse tells us what we should follow after, or how we should live our lives, and if we let Christ live through us, we will live the righteous life we should live. If Christians would just read the bible (Romans 12:2), and know how Jesus lived His life, we could do the same, not to be right with God or earn anything, but because we love God and Jesus, and want to live a holy life to glorify them (1 Peter 1:16). When we walk after the spirit, instead of after the flesh (Romans 8:4), we let Jesus live through us, and we don’t have to try and be holy, as He is already holy. If you are truly a born again Christian (little Christ), then you must let Him live through you, and not try to be like Him through human effort. No one can truly live a holy life, except Christ live in you (Galatians 4:6) and through you. Praise God for the indwelling Spirit of Christ (Romans 8:10) to live in the born again Christian!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
